newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain prices seen unmoved by duty change.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain prices seen unmoved by duty change.

text.p: Polish grain prices are not expected to rise after Poland reinstalls its 20 percent customs duties on July 1 because the country has large reserves and does not need imports, the agiculture ministry said on Monday.
"We have a surplus of grain and that is why grain prices will not be affected by the reinstalled customs duties," Malgorzata Ksiazyk, the ministry's spokeswoman told Reuters.
The government suspended duties on most grains and rapeseed late last year before partly reinstalling them in early 1997.
Polish grain production in 1997 was seen flat or be just lower than last year's output of 24.73 million tonnes.
On July 1 Poland will also reinstall 15 percent duties on rapeseed imports. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
